proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the hospitalization process has dynamics not well-approximated by a fixed 2-week lag (e.g., variable lag or additional smoothing), forecasts may show phase error around the peak and mis-timed decline.
proposals.rationale: Matches prior discovered pattern and surveillance note that admissions lag an infectious proxy; SEIRS supports sharp seasonal peaks via waning immunity while remaining parsimonious for a 31-week training window.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is longer (or effectively longer due to reporting delays), the model may peak too early and overpredict near-term rates.
proposals.rationale: Alternative shorter lag to hedge timing uncertainty in older-adult admissions; retains SEIRS flexibility for high peakiness while keeping the observation model simple.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is shorter, the model may peak too late and underpredict the early upswing.
proposals.rationale: Alternative longer lag to capture slower progression-to-admission in older adults and/or reporting latency; still parsimonious compared with adding an explicit H compartment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, leading to parameter tradeoffs (E/I/H rates) and unstable extrapolation beyond the peak.
proposals.rationale: Directly aligns the observation with the hospitalization-rate target via an explicit H compartment; can better represent admission/occupancy dynamics than a pure lagged-I proxy when peakiness is high.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the target is closer to pure admissions than a mixture, the model may fit by compensating with unrealistic I/H proportions, degrading peak height and tail behavior.
proposals.rationale: Robustifies against ambiguity between incident infectious burden and hospitalized burden by allowing the observation to reflect a mixture; can reduce sensitivity to H identifiability while still leveraging SEIHR structure.
